changes: Third guide raise: FY26 revenue $4.4bn to $4.6bn (from $3.9bn to $4.2bn), non-GAAP operating income $960mn to $1,030mn, EPS $3.10 to $3.40; implied 4Q revenue $1.35bn to $1.55bn vs $1.21bn consensus.
Clean margin stepped up: non-GAAP gross margin 34.5% with no material tariff recovery in the quarter, against 30.8% on a clean basis in 2Q26; product margin 38.4%.
Growth now consumes cash: operating cash flow -$27.1mn and FCF -$180.6mn, as contract assets rose $430.3mn and inventory $170.4mn; net cash of about $137mn at 30 June became about $39mn of net debt.
Concentration fell but shifted to the financier: the largest customer was 43% of revenue (73% in 2Q26), and a Brookfield related-party vehicle was 26%.
Still no backlog number: RPO rose 49% to $661.2mn, but management deferred any backlog figure to 4Q guidance, and Jupiter was not mentioned on the call.
checks: Primary figures were taken from the 3Q26 8-K Ex.99.1, the supplemental slides and the 3Q26 10-Q, downloaded from EDGAR and converted to text; 2Q26 comparatives and consensus come from the 22 October consensus card (itself verified against EDGAR and consensus pages). Derived numbers (growth rates, implied 4Q revenue and operating income from FY guide minus 9M, FCF, net debt on a principal basis, P/E at the pre-market price, 4Q OCF needed for the $375mn baseline) were recomputed in Python (scripts/calc_be.py). An independent subagent that had not seen the reasoning rechecked every figure against the release, 10-Q, both 3Q26 transcripts (Motley Fool, Investing.com), the 2Q26 transcript and StockAnalysis prices, and confirmed all P&L, cash-flow, balance-sheet, debt and 10-Q quotes. It found and I corrected: the takeaway's 9% (revenue; EPS midpoint is about 20% above consensus), opex share (about 11%, not 12%), 2Q26 permit questions (none), the 5 GW wording (management called 5 GW 'a milestone'; 'approaching 5 GW' is a transcript provider's summary), the CFO's expectation of positive FCF, and the 30 June contract-asset balance ($428.3mn). Caveats: Jupiter hearing (7 December) and pipeline (February 2027) dates come from secondary press via the preview card; the related-party customer is identified as the Brookfield vehicle by inference from the 10-Q's customer definition; Hunterbrook is named only in press; 2Q26 Q&A comes from one transcript provider; Q&A counts are judgment calls. Share prices: 22 October close and after-hours and 23 October 9:08 am ET pre-market (StockAnalysis, Investing.com). No convertible price or CDS was found.
consensus_thesis: Investors own Bloom as the default supplier of fast, on-site, non-combustion power for AI data centers and pay about 42x FY27 consensus EPS for revenue doubling in FY26 and rising about 63% in FY27 at mid-30s margins.
headline: The consensus view holds and FY26 earnings power is higher than modelled (guide midpoints about 9% above revenue and 20% above EPS consensus), but growth is now financed by Bloom's own working capital, so the stock should be judged on cash conversion and a disclosed backlog rather than on revenue beats; credit quality holds for now on $2.5bn of cash and 0% notes, but the net-cash cushion is gone.
kona: Bloom's 10-Q makes explicit what the Jupiter story implied: financiers will not buy on-site power equipment until permits are in hand, and the supplier carries the working capital in between (contract assets up $430mn in one quarter). For Kona, the air permit and firm gas supply are financing conditions, not just construction steps, and should be in hand before equipment is ordered on credit. If Kona buys fuel cells or gensets, expect deposit-heavy terms (Bloom's customer deposits rose to $661mn from $78mn this year); if Kona sells power, Bloom's buyers show that a financier-owned, PPA-backed structure works only with a creditworthy offtaker.
monitor: 4Q26 operating cash flow of at least about $102mn (the CFO's '$375mn-plus' FY baseline) and conversion of $858.6mn of contract assets.

sections.body: Debt: $2.5bn 0% convertible notes due November 2030 (conversion $194.97, about 12.8mn shares) and $22.8mn 3% Green Notes due 2029; nothing drawn on the $600mn revolver, whose $90mn letter-of-credit sub-facility is fully used. No maturities in the next 24 months beyond a $3.0mn Korean JV loan. The next dollar: management says it may 'enter the equity or debt market as needed' and may use equipment lease financing for capex (10-Q). Per share: diluted weighted shares 324.3mn; the converts are in the money at $209.80, so settlement policy matters for dilution. Credit read: liquidity is ample, but Bloom now carries its buyers' working capital; a second negative cash quarter would turn the 0% notes from a cheap option into the main funding source. Earnings per share are rising faster than cash per share; the gap is the financing Bloom provides to its customers' financiers.

sections.title: Monitoring checklist

head: Question
Why it matters / asked on the call
rows: Backlog (equity). You say backlog grows faster than revenue, yet RPO is $661.2mn against FY27 consensus of $6.71bn, and you deferred any figure to 4Q. Will the 4Q disclosure show firm orders with deposits, in GW and dollars, scheduled for 2027? Do they cover more or less than half of FY27 consensus, yes or no?
Asked by Mizuho; deflected. The share price rests on FY27.

Contract assets (credit). Contract assets reached $858.6mn and receivables $634.7mn; three customers hold 70% of receivables, the largest a related party. What share is owed by Brookfield or other financing vehicles, and when do the milestones bill? Will you commit to a FY26 OCF figure?
Asked by Evercore and Oppenheimer; partial. Profit in receivables is the first sign of a funding need.

Permits (credit and equity). The 10-Q says you generally cannot sell to a financier until permits are in hand. How much of the implied $1.35bn-$1.55bn 4Q depends on permits not yet issued, and is any of it Jupiter?
Not asked. It turns a regulatory calendar into a revenue calendar.
Related party (credit). The Brookfield vehicle was 26% of 3Q revenue. What equity, guarantees or price concessions does Bloom provide to it, and what is its own funding capacity for 2027?
Not asked. A financier's balance sheet now drives a quarter of revenue.

Convertibles (credit). The 0% 2030 notes convert at $194.97, below the share price. Will you settle conversions in cash or shares, and would you use the notes' headroom or new equity to fund working capital?
Not asked. It decides dilution versus liquidity.
